description: Nigeria STR work visa (Subject to Regularisation) help for UK residents taking up a job in Nigeria. Approval, documents and your application.
h1: Nigeria STR work visa from the UK
intro: The Nigeria STR work visa (Subject to Regularisation) is the visa for taking up long-term employment in Nigeria. Your employer obtains approval first, then you apply from the UK, and you regularise your status after you arrive.
eligibility: You have a job offer from an employer in Nigeria
Your employer has obtained, or is applying for, STR approval from the Nigeria Immigration Service
You are taking up long-term employment, not a short assignment

sections.heading: How the Nigeria STR work visa works
sections.text:
Getting a Nigeria STR visa is a staged process:
- Your employer in Nigeria applies to the Nigeria Immigration Service for approval to employ you
- Once approval is granted, you apply for the STR visa from the UK, with the approval letter and your documents
- After you arrive in Nigeria, you regularise your status and obtain your residence permit, known as CERPAC, within the time allowed

sections.heading: Documents for a Nigeria STR visa
sections.text: Your employer usually provides the approval letter and your employment documents. You provide your passport, photos, CV and qualifications. Degree certificates sometimes need to be legalised first, which we can arrange.

sections.heading: STR visa or Temporary Work Permit?
sections.text: The STR visa is for long-term jobs. If you're going to Nigeria for a short specialist assignment, such as installing or repairing equipment, a [Temporary Work Permit](/nigeria-temporary-work-permit-uk/) is usually the right route instead.

sections.heading: Nigeria STR visa help from Manchester
sections.text: We help UK residents and employers with Nigeria STR visa applications, checking your approval and documents before you apply. Requirements can change, so we confirm the current process for your application.

faqs.a: Subject to Regularisation. You enter Nigeria on the STR visa and then regularise your status by obtaining a residence permit.
Your employer in Nigeria applies to the Nigeria Immigration Service. You apply for the visa once approval is granted.

faqs.q: Can I work in Nigeria on a business eVisa?
faqs.a: No. Taking up employment in Nigeria needs the right work visa, such as the STR visa.
